passage: Last week I had a cold, and my voice came out nasal and rough. When I answered in class, Nandini copied me in a silly voice and some kids laughed. My face went hot. I wanted to say, “It's my cold!” but nothing came. That evening Mummy gave me warm water and said the voice was because my nose was blocked and my throat was sore. It was my body, not my mood. Next day I told Nandini, “I'm not sad or grumpy, I'm just sick.” She looked ashamed and said sorry. I'm Farida, and I understand my voice a bit better now.

qa.q: What did Nandini do when Farida answered in class?
qa.a: She copied Farida in a silly voice.

qa.q: How did Farida feel when the class laughed, and how do you know?
qa.a: Farida felt embarrassed, since Farida's face went hot and words to explain would not come.

qa.q: What did Farida do that helped clear things up?
qa.a: Farida told Nandini it was a cold, not sadness or grumpiness, which explained the voice.

qa.q: Why might Nandini have misread Farida's voice?
qa.a: Nandini may have thought the strange voice meant a mood or was just funny, without thinking it came from a cold.

grounding: A nasal, raspy voice reflects a cold and body state, not mood, and mocking it is a misreading.

passage: Counsellor's note, Class 5. Dilnaz came to see me because some classmates called her voice “angry crow.” Her voice has been raspy for four days after cheering at the sports day. She wondered aloud if she sounded mean. I explained that a raspy voice usually tells us something about the throat, not the feelings, and that a doctor could look if it keeps going or worries her. With her permission, I spoke to Maria, who had joined in the teasing. Maria said she had assumed Dilnaz was grumpy. She agreed to apologise. Dilnaz drank water and left smiling a little. Ms. Maria's class will hear a short talk on voices. Counsellor.

qa.q: How long has Dilnaz's voice been raspy?
What was Dilnaz worried about when she came to the counsellor?
qa.a: She wondered whether her raspy voice made her sound mean to others.

qa.q: What could Dilnaz do if the raspy voice keeps going?
qa.a: She could tell a trusted adult and check with the doctor if it keeps going or worries her.

qa.q: Why might Maria have joined in the teasing?
qa.a: Maria assumed Dilnaz was grumpy because of how she sounded, so she read a body state as a mood.

grounding: A raspy voice from shouting reflects body state, peers misread it as mood, and an adult teaches that voice quality is body first.
